text: No major provider ships just one model. Anthropic currently offers four tiers at once, from fastest to most capable — and that's not marketing fragmentation, it's a real, unavoidable trade-off.

Here's Anthropic's actual current lineup, by their own description. Haiku: the fastest model with near-frontier intelligence. Sonnet: the best combination of speed and intelligence. Opus: for long-running agentic coding and knowledge work. Fable: for demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work. Four tiers, four different jobs.

And the pricing tracks it exactly. Haiku: one dollar in, five dollars out, per million tokens — fastest. Sonnet: two and ten — fast. Opus: four and twenty — moderate. Fable: ten and fifty — slower. Price and latency climb together as capability goes up. This exact pattern — cheap tier, balanced tier, flagship tier — shows up at every major provider, just with different names.

Anthropic's own documentation gives two honest starting strategies. Efficiency-first: start cheap and fast, test thoroughly, upgrade only if you hit a real capability gap. Capability-first: start with the strongest model for a genuinely hard task, then look for room to downgrade once you understand what it actually needs. Neither one says always reach for the biggest model.

A flagship model costs more and responds slower — not a rounding error at scale, especially for high-volume, simple work. The real skill is matching task difficulty to tier. Next lesson: why even the most capable model still sometimes confidently makes things up.
